name: Nimbus-Tide
description: Nimbus-Tide is a cool oceanic world where towering cloud formations descend so low they merge with the wave crests, creating a layered realm where sea and sky become indistinguishable. The ocean is shallow compared to most water worlds, averaging only three kilometers in depth, with volcanic island chains breaking the surface in long, curving arcs. Tidal forces from two close moons create dramatic water level changes that reshape coastlines daily.

The boundaries between ocean, cloud, and air dissolve into each other in ways that disorient newcomers. Swimming upward can feel like flying, and the fog banks that roll between the island chains are so dense that visibility drops to arm's length. The fauna has adapted to this liminal environment, with species that transition effortlessly between aquatic and aerial locomotion, their translucent bodies glowing with borrowed bioluminescence.

An ancient navigation beacon operates on the tallest volcanic peak, broadcasting coordinates and atmospheric data in a format that took linguists years to decode. The beacon's power source remains unknown, drawing no measurable energy from any identifiable mechanism yet maintaining a signal strong enough to reach neighboring star systems. Its placement suggests it was intended to guide ships to this world specifically.

Nimbus-Tide's medicinal fauna, organisms that produce compounds effective against radiation poisoning, have made the planet medically significant. The beacon draws a steady stream of researchers hoping to trace its origin, while the unique environment attracts extreme tourism operators. But the tidal extremes and disorienting fog have claimed numerous vessels, and the ocean floor is littered with wrecks from those who underestimated the planet's deceptive gentleness.
